audits.title: 78 A Quality Improvement Project on Oxygen Administration Within the Geriatrics COVID-19 Cohort Ward
audits.standard: Documented oxygen therapy on observation charts (device, flow rate, target saturations)
audits.setting: Geriatrics COVID-19 cohort ward, Whiston Hospital
audits.intervention: Staff education session, bedside oxygen guideline posters, quiz and reminder lanyard cards over 4 PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 100% correct oxygen device and flow rate after the 2nd and 3rd PDSA cycles.

audits.other_findings: All staff reported greater confidence in oxygen management after teaching.
audits.citation: Hickson L, Liu A, Bailey G, Bruce S, Kawafi K, Reid D, et al.. 78 A Quality Improvement Project on Oxygen Administration Within the Geriatrics COVID-19 Cohort Ward. Age Ageing. 2021;50(Suppl 1):i12-i42.

audits.title: Oxygen therapy multicentric study--a nationwide audit to oxygen therapy procedures in internal medicine wards.
audits.standard: BTS guideline for emergency oxygen use in adult patients

cycle1.result: Oxygen prescribed in 93.4%; 82.4% fixed dose but only 11.6% of those complete; oxygen given to only 77.0% with fixed-dose prescriptions; FiO2/flow and device matched in 70.9% and 89.2%; 82.7% of 127 target-range prescriptions within range.

audits.other_findings: Missing duration and monitoring were the commonest errors; target saturation prescribing still a minority.
audits.citation: Neves JT, Lobão MJ, Grupo de trabalho EMO. Oxygen therapy multicentric study--a nationwide audit to oxygen therapy procedures in internal medicine wards. Rev Port Pneumol. 2012;18(2):80-85. doi:10.1016/j.rppneu.2012.01.001. PMID: 22280829.

audits.title: A new oxygen prescription produces real improvements in therapeutic oxygen use.
audits.standard: British Thoracic Society oxygen audit standards (four key standards)
audits.setting: Acute Medical Unit, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 55% had a valid oxygen prescription; 50% had a documented target saturation range; 84% had saturations on the MEWS chart; 0% had oxygen signed for at drug rounds.

audits.intervention: New oxygen prescription chart, oxygen alert stickers for drug and MEWS charts, point-of-care resources and senior-led education, over three PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: After PDSA cycle three: valid prescription 94%, target range documented 94%, saturations on MEWS chart 100%, oxygen signed for at drug rounds 18%.

audits.other_findings: Signing for oxygen at drug rounds remained poor; Trust-wide rollout projected to save £30,400 a year.
audits.citation: Rudge J, Odedra S, Harrison D. A new oxygen prescription produces real improvements in therapeutic oxygen use. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2014;3(1):u204031.w1815. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u204031.w1815. PMID: 26734309.

audits.title: Acute oxygen therapy: an audit of prescribing and delivery practices in a tertiary hospital in Perth, Western Australia.
audits.standard: Oxygen prescription guidelines with appropriate medically indicated target saturations
audits.setting: Acute Medical Unit, Royal Perth Hospital

cycle1.result: 36 of 65 (55.4%) had target oxygen saturations prescribed and 25% of prescribed targets were inappropriate; 49 (75.4%) exposed to potential risk from prescription and/or delivery error.

audits.other_findings: A real risk was identified in 19 patients (29.2%) who received oxygen outside their appropriate target range.
audits.citation: Kamran A, Chia E, Tobin C. Acute oxygen therapy: an audit of prescribing and delivery practices in a tertiary hospital in Perth, Western Australia. Intern Med J. 2018;48(2):151-157. doi:10.1111/imj.13612. PMID: 28869712.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Acute Oxygen Therapy: Enhancing Patient Care at Dammar Teaching Hospital.
audits.standard: Oxygen therapy guidelines (nine parameters including device flow rates, documentation and weaning)

cycle1.result: Correct nasal cannula use 50.0%; non-rebreather 61.9%; target SpO2 recorded in type 2 respiratory failure 69.0%; routine SpO2 monitoring 50.0%; immediate oxygen for at-risk patients 16.7%; weaning 76.2%; timely discontinuation 78.6%.

cycle2.result: Nasal cannula 92.3%; non-rebreather 100.0%; target SpO2 recorded 100.0%; SpO2 monitoring 82.1%; immediate oxygen 70.0%; weaning 45.0%; timely discontinuation 47.5%.

audits.other_findings: Weaning and discontinuation compliance fell after the intervention.
audits.citation: Mohammed Albadwy MTE, Elshaikh SA, Ahmed A, Hamed FJM, Ahmed A, Elzain Abdalla MS, et al.. Clinical Audit of Acute Oxygen Therapy: Enhancing Patient Care at Dammar Teaching Hospital. Cureus. 2025;17(9):e92790. doi:10.7759/cureus.92790. PMID: 41127747.

audits.title: An audit of the prescribing, administering and monitoring of oxygen therapy within a hospice
audits.standard: Local hospice oxygen guideline based on BTS emergency oxygen guideline 2008

cycle1.result: 60% of oxygen prescriptions signed and dated; delivery system and flow rate recorded at drug rounds in 19%.

audits.intervention: Results disseminated to the team; oxygen charts amended to show who completes each section; prompt added to the main drug chart.

cycle2.result: 100% of oxygen prescriptions signed and dated; delivery system and flow rate recorded in 61%.

audits.other_findings: Nurses mostly stopped checking saturations when not indicated.
audits.citation: Foster G. An audit of the prescribing, administering and monitoring of oxygen therapy within a hospice. BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care. 2012;2(Suppl 1):A62.1-A62. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2012-000196.180.
